end.summary:
Named radius, chord, diameter, arc, segment, and sector through examples.
Related radius, diameter, and chord lengths, including that a diameter is the longest chord.
Described rotational symmetry of a circle at every angle.
Initially said a circle had four lines of symmetry, then revised this to infinitely many using diameters.
Teach-back was not completed successfully.
end.parentNote: Dev practised circle-part definitions, chord and diameter relationships, and reflection and rotation symmetry. They used the “slice” idea for a sector and the “straight cut” idea for a segment, and corrected the initial four-lines-of-symmetry mix-up later by noting that every diameter gives a line of symmetry. At home, ask Dev to label a circle with radius, chord, diameter, arc, segment, and sector, then explain why a circle has infinitely many lines of symmetry.
